chapter: Technique and life on the road (repeated passages)
title: A famous trombonist in Hawaii and Sandy Williams's badly fitted teeth
summary: He praises an unnamed famous trombonist living in Hawaii, and says Sandy Williams stopped playing over an improper fit, urging musicians to find a dentist who understands them.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Trombone too. Don't forget that. The very famous one -- I won't name the name. He probably don't want nobody to know that he -- but he brags it to me about it but maybe he don't want everybody to know about it. So there you go. But he ain't got a child in the yard up there but he still -- he still hits the scene man. And beautiful.
Sounds as good as he did if not better. You know.
Do you think maybe off the record we could say who he was.
Oh you wouldn't know who he was. He lives in Hawaii -- should I say anymore.
Oh, yeah. Yeah. Oh yeah, he's a beautiful -- out in Colorado he sounded very good.
Sure. Plays just as good if not better. I dig it. And there's a guy named Sandy Williams. Just Sandy. He's scared to blow because he's scared of his teeth. But he got a improper fit.

You see you must have a proper fit made. You've got to make your mouth look as it did when you had teeth you know. And not the guy to fix those teeth so that your nose is the same distance from your chin as it was at first you know. Particularly those little bitty mash teeth. Little bitty teeth and make your mouth too short and then you can't -- you can't work that that way you know.
You ain't got enough chops for the big mouthpiece. You know. So if you could get a dentist that's interested -- you got to get a dentist interested in your particular mouth.
Yeah. And a dentist who realizes that you're a musician.
Yeah, that's your livelihood you know.
Yeah. Yeah, Sandy was a helluva trombone player too.

Sure. Sure he was. And he still could be. He just put his arm down cause he got scared he couldn't play. So if you don't play, how are you going to play if you don't play? You know. All you have to do is get the

right fit teeth. Don't let them slam anything to you. Say now this ain't right,man, fix them. Make those teeth a little bigger. And make my mouth and my nose so I won't look all scrunched up to the mouth -- you know. You know what I mean? And give me some sturdy teeth cause you've got to have them sturdy. You know what I mean?
It can be done. It's been done and it is done.
Well, they do those things better now than they used to --
Sure they do, and there shouldn't be no problem anymore.
